evals.prompt: Council this design proposal before we write code. Do not implement anything.
evals.expected_output: Dispatch the latest flagship model of three different providers (for example Claude Opus, GPT Sol and the latest Gemini) at high effort, unless the user named members. Review the proposal directly, keep work read-only and summarize useful findings and disagreements. No commit or exact-SHA gate is needed.

evals.prompt: Council this code change. The user named Gemini Neon as a member, but it cannot run. Can you use another Gemini model instead?
evals.expected_output: Report the named member as unavailable instead of substituting another model.

evals.prompt: The council has completed two code-review passes for an open PR, and one reviewer omitted its score. Where do the results go?
evals.expected_output: Update the PR description with the round count and a per-delegate, per-round score table before the model/harness line. Use no score for the missing value, do not invent it and do not add a comment just for this report.

evals.prompt: Council round 1 left two findings, which you fixed. What happens next?
evals.expected_output: Request a fresh review from the delegates; it counts as a new round. Continue until all delegates are satisfied, while fighting scope creep. Round caps or a single follow-up reviewer apply only when the user asks for them.

evals.prompt: Council round 1 has two delegates still running on the shared checkout, and one delegate already returned findings. The user also marked one delegate non-blocking. What should you do?
evals.expected_output: Check the arriving findings against the code immediately and decide what to fix without waiting idle, but do not edit files while another delegate is still reviewing the same checkout. Do not wait for the non-blocking delegate; if it returns late, treat it as feedback and do not record its score.
